description: Probability that a lot gets built within 5 years. Use with feasim: margin R = value of new project / (cost excluding land + parcel's current assessed land + building value).

existing_house_curve.formula: P5 = 1 - (1 - 1/(1 + exp(-z)))^5, z = a + b*ln(R) + c*owner_occupied + d*ln(B/L) + e*steep + f*extreme_tsunami_zone + g*sea_level_rise_3.2ft_zone  (z is the log-odds of the annual probability)

terms.R: profit ratio from the pro forma (new value / (cost + current land and building value))
terms.ln(B/L): assessed building value / land value; typical Oahu lot 0.32
terms.steep: 10 m USGS slope at the lot centroid >= 20% (11.5% of Oahu lots)
terms.sea_level_rise_3.2ft_zone: State Hazards layer 15 (1% coastal flood with 3.2 ft sea level rise)

existing_house_curve.held_out: out-of-sample log loss, 5-fold by plat, 3 repeats: profit+owner 3444.4 -> +B/L 3430.9 -> +steep+coastal 3417.3
existing_house_curve.fitted_on: Oahu single-family-zoned lots with an existing house, 2022 roll vs new-home permits Jan 2022 - Jun 2025 (115,114 lots, 606 rebuilt), annual hazard over 3.5 years
existing_house_curve.other_islands: borrowed from Oahu; Maui confirms the owner-occupancy effect; slope and hazard flags are available statewide

a_Kauai.basis: interpolated: mean and range of the town-type islands (Oahu, Maui, Hawaii Co RS/RD); permits per resident did not order the islands

vacant_lot.cost_rule: each island's hard cost per sq ft set so its median vacant lot has R = 1 (Oahu $150, Maui $123, Hawaii Co towns $92, rural $38)
vacant_lot.outcome: home completed and recorded on the assessment roll (Oahu 2022->2026, Maui 2020->2025, Hawaii Co ~2022->2026)
vacant_lot.tests: one shared slope beats a flat rate and fits as well as separate slopes, held out by plat across all four island areas; Maui alone is close to flat (44 builds)

developer_controlled_5yr.caution: those lots were identified by clusters of building in the same window, so the rate is biased upward by construction. Prefer the approved-project rate, or count subdivisions by each project's own schedule.

approved_project_5yr.basis: 13 Council-approved 201H projects 2019-21 (DPP status report, Feb 2024). Oahu only; borrowed for other islands. Of 13 approved 2022-24, 1 had a permit by Feb 2024.

market_conditions_multiplier.basis: 2022-mid 2025 was a slow stretch: rebuilding on existing Oahu lots ran at 76% of its 2005-2025 average. Multiply the curve by this to get a typical five years; the range is the 10th-90th percentile of 5-year windows since 2005. Assumes the slowdown hit all profit levels proportionally.

not_covered: apartment and business zones (too few 2022-25 events to fit; the TOD, parking and fee scenarios currently borrow the single-family curve)
which specific lots get built: use expected units = sum of P5 x net new units

tested_and_rejected.FEMA_flood_zone: no effect on Oahu rebuilds (multiplier 0.93, worse held-out); none on vacant lots
tested_and_rejected.slope_on_vacant_lots: no held-out gain (land value already reflects it)
tested_and_rejected.lava_zones_Hawaii_County: zones 1-2 and 3 slightly lower (0.88, 0.84) but held-out gain is marginal; not used
tested_and_rejected.high_fire_risk: vacant lots in high fire-risk areas are built more often (1.3x), which reflects where growth is (dry leeward areas), not fire; not used because it would imply hazard attracts building
